recipes.name: Cauliflower Custard
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon butter for greasing, or as needed
1 head cauliflower, separated into small florets

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place cauliflower in a saucepan and cover with water and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer until cauliflower is tender, 10 to 15 minutes; drain and transfer cauliflower to prepared casserole dish.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and parsley in the melted butter until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes.
Slowing pour 1 cup milk into flour mixture. Cook and stir milk mixture until thickened, 3 to 5 minutes; pour over cauliflower.
Whisk eggs, 1 cup milk, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and white pepper in a bowl; pour over cauliflower mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until the custard is set, 30 to 35 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Cauliflower Custard
raw_recipe.description: A savory custard vegetable side dish that is different and delicious. The result is a creamed-custard cauliflower sensation that even the pickiest children enjoy!

review.reviewBody: I'm giving this five stars because I honestly wasn't expecting this to turn out that great but it DID! I made it exactly as written, the only change I made was to add half a chopped onion.

I made this and we loved it. I was concerned with all of the comments about it being bland so I followed many of the suggested tips. Adding garlic to every step, onion, etc. A major difference that I did was add a bay leaf when I boiled the cauliflower. That was a big win and added the perfect amount of flavor (along with the other modifications others mentioned). I made this 3 days ago and we KEEP TALKING ABOUT IT. I’ve saved this and will be adding this to my regular side rotation. Oh and super easy too!

This review may not be completely fair because I tweaked the recipe for a lectin-free eat.

I replaced the butter with my bacon lard, milk with canned coconut milk, used oregano instead of parsley, tapioca flour instead of flour, excluded the white pepper, and added garlic powder to pretty much every cooking step as suggested with additional oregano in the egg-milk mixture.

After I boiled the cauliflower, I should've let it strain for longer. the custard was a bit watery.

The casserole was decent, but kinda lacking in flavor. The fried butter topping was by far the tastiest part (love it). If I make this again, I am definately going to add some sort of spice to the egg-milk mixture for a better taste or coat the boiled cauliflower with herbs.

Not bad as a base recipe!

I am rating recipe as I made it, not as written. Based on the suggestions in the previous review, I added half a sauteed onion to the cauliflower, put garlic salt in all three steps, added a little red pepper and upped the parsley significantly. Tasty!

This was really lacking in flavor. Not delicate, not plain, not simple....it was bland. With some garlic/onion/hot sauce this could definitely be a 5 star dish. The texture was fabulous and the ease of preparation was refreshing-no canned soups, processed cheese, etc. If I make this again, I would definitely add a lot more flavoring agents. Thanks for a no fuss--no massively processed food ingredient casserole! Though their favorite cauliflower recipe is Roasted Garlic Cauliflower from this site...my eaters enjoyed it too, so it's in the keeper box.

Edit: made it again for a better picture and it never set. Literally the custard set in top but the bottom was a runny mess. Used purple cauliflower as that is what we had. Added dried shallots and roasted garlic powder for flavor.
I liked the fact that this wasn't a cheesy dish. The sauce is good, though I did reduce the milk a little and added sautéed onions and mushrooms
I think I did this wrong. The egg mixture was sort of runny on the bottom and didn't blend with the flower mixture. Overall it was very bland.
This was delicious. The family loved it.
It was OK , not enough flavor for us. will not make again.

this recipe was not precise enough for me! For example how much Cauliflower ?I substituted dill for the parsley and added a eighth of a teaspoon of cayenne pepper because we like it spicy but I would not make it again!
This recipe was just delicious and is definitely a keeper. I followed the recipe exactly and my whole family loved it, even the toddlers! Thank you for a wonderful recipe!
I loved this! I halved the recipe and only used 1 egg. It turned out great!
